title: Curate, publish, and maintain Redwood-verified performance profiles with lifecycle playbook
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Goal: Establish a repeatable, auditable playbook to publish and maintain Redwood-verified performance profiles (latency, throughput, cost) for model families and specific version pins. This ticket scopes the curation process, automation hooks, governance gates, and required artifacts so that downstream teams (SDK, Console, Dedicated) can rely on stable published profiles for routing and recommendations.

Background: We already run ad-hoc benchmarking during model onboarding but lack a standardized lifecycle: profiles go stale as kernels, infra, and quantization options evolve. This causes inaccurate cost/latency guidance in the Console and occasional customer regressions when automatic routing uses an out-of-date profile. The playbook will reduce regression risk, speed onboarding, and enable scheduled revalidation jobs tied to infra/quantization/driver changes.
acceptance_criteria: A documented playbook (Confluence) exists that describes required artifacts for publishing a verified profile: test harness configuration, dataset prompts, traffic distribution, sequence lengths, cost model parameters, and environment spec.
An automated pipeline in CI that executes the reference perf runs and writes a candidate profile JSON to S3 with tags for model, version, hardware, quantization, and kernel config.
A human review step (PM + Runtime SME) gated in the pipeline for final publish to the Performance Profile Catalog; publish action creates a manifest entry consumed by runtime and Console.
Profiles include metadata for reproducibility (git commit, docker image, driver version, run timestamp) and a unique profile_id for pinning in customer-facing features.
Rollforward and rollback procedures defined: how to deprecate a profile, replace it with a newer profile, and how automatic routing falls back to compatible variants.
Smoke-monitoring dashboards updated (per-profile latency/cost), and alerts configured for >10% drift vs published median latency or >15% cost delta on production traffic buckets.
At least two models (one encoder-decoder, one decoder-only) have been published via the new workflow as a proof-of-concept and linked in the ticket.
implementation_plan: Define canonical benchmark suite and fixture prompts (PM + Research) and check into /infra/benchmarks/reference-prompts in repo.
Add CI job that runs candidate perf runs on a reproducible infra image and uploads results to s3://redwood-perf-candidates/<model>/<version>/<run_id>.json.
Implement a lightweight review UI in Console under 'Profile Catalog' to approve/reject candidate profiles; approvals create 'published' manifests consumed by router.

Schema for profile JSON and manifest: fields for median P50/P95 latency, throughput at target batch sizes, cost-per-token estimate, hardware footprint, and compatibility tags (quantization, dtype, kernel-features).
Instrumentation: attach provenance (git sha, container digest, host driver) and attach a perf-run artifact (raw samples + aggregated metrics) for auditing.
Create a scheduled revalidation job that re-runs profiles weekly for high-traffic models and monthly for others, with automatic candidate create and an alert on large drift.
Define owner responsibilities and SLAs for profile updates: Runtime owns revalidation infra; PMs own prompt sets and acceptance criteria; Research owns statistical methodology.
testing_harness: Reference harness: a dockerized job (registry.redwood.com/perf/harness:2026.01) that accepts a model binary, run config (seq lengths, batch distribution), and outputs a profile JSON. The harness includes stable RNG seeds, synthetic and sampled prompt mixes, and KV-cache warmup rules to ensure reproducibility. A local dev command 'tools/perf/run_profile.sh' reproduces CI runs for debugging.
rollout_and_governance: Publish flow: candidate -> internal review -> published manifest -> router/console pick up. Governance gates: security review for non-open models, Runtime SME sign-off for kernel/driver differences, and PM acceptance for cost/quality tradeoffs. Deprecation policy: profiles older than 9 months are flagged; if revalidation fails twice, profile is auto-deprecated and traffic is routed to the next compatible model variant per fallback policy.
monitoring_and_alerting: Per-profile dashboards in Console showing P50/P95 latency, tokens/sec, error-rate, and estimated cost-per-1M-tokens.
Drift alert: triggered when observed P50 latency deviates >10% from published P50 over a 1-hour window for a steady traffic bucket.
Cost alert: triggered when effective cost-per-token increases >15% vs published estimate for 24h window.
Profile health heartbeat: daily job to verify publishing manifest integrity and last-validation timestamp; alerts if missing.
notes: Design note: Console UI copy should emphasize reproducibility metadata so customers can reason about profiles when choosing pinned versions.
We need a lightweight storage schema: profile manifest for lookup and full artifacts stored in S3 with retention policy of 18 months for auditability.
Cost-model calibration: Research to provide a mapping from GPU time + memory footprint to estimated $/token for each cloud region used by hosted API.
Legal: Customer-facing language around 'verified' should be vetted by Comms and Legal to avoid commitments beyond tested conditions.
